name: The St. Regis Langkawi
positioning: Beachfront St. Regis resort on a lagoon at the southeast tip of Langkawi, with four over-water villas and an over-water restaurant on the Andaman Sea
best_for: Couples who want an over-water villa with its own infinity pool
Travelers who want a beach resort with several restaurants and bars on site

facts.text: The resort is located in UNESCO's first Southeast Asia Geopark, known for its 99-island archipelago.
The resort is at the southeast tip of the island, surrounded by centuries-old rainforest.
Interiors were designed by G.A Design and the architecture by Gensler, in a classical contemporary style with European and Middle Eastern influences.
All rooms offer unobstructed sea views from their terraces.
Rooms feature bold accent hues and paintings by local artists.
The Sunset Over-Water Villa has separate living and dining rooms, a kitchenette and a walk-in wardrobe.
L'Orangerie is a beachfront restaurant serving a fusion of modern French cuisine and Asian flavours.
Pantai Grill serves seafood and steaks cooked over a wood-fire grill.
The St. Regis Bar has a live band each evening.
Afternoon tea is served in the Drawing Room in the lobby, with fine teas and classic sweets and savouries with a local twist.
The resort has an outdoor infinity pool, and spa treatments are infused with tropical botanicals.
The resort offers the signature St. Regis butler service.

highlights.text: There are four over-water villas: three Sunset Overwater Villas and the Sunset Royal Villa, each with a private terrace and infinity pool.
The resort sits on the largest lagoon, with a 600-meter white sand beach facing the Andaman Sea.
Kayuputi, the over-water restaurant, is designed as an art collector's beach house and serves pan-Asian inspired cuisine.
The St. Regis Bar serves the Lang Mary, a twist on the Bloody Mary named after the 'island of the reddish-brown eagle' in Malay.
The St. Regis Bar features an installation of banyan tree bark, sculpted trunks and suspended leaves set against a granite wall.

considerations.text: Langkawi International Airport is about 12.6 km away, and the hotel does not provide a shuttle service.
Pets are not allowed, and guests are encouraged to dress smart casual from breakfast through dinner.
WhataHotel notes that the remote island location requires additional travel planning.
